body:
For each procedure, discuss whether it can be described in the choice model and whether it is compatible with the rational man paradigm:

  1. a

    the decision maker maximizes another person’s suffering;

  2. b

    he asks his two children to rank the alternatives and chooses the one with the lowest average score;

  3. c

    he has an ideal point in mind and chooses the alternative closest to it according to some distance function;

  4. d

    he looks for the alternative that appears most often in the choice set;

  5. e

    he has an ordering of X in mind and always chooses the median element.

Answer

(a) Rational: the choice function is rationalized by ≿ itself, whatever it ranks. (b) Not rational in general: a counterexample is machine-checked. (c) Rational, for any real-valued “distance”. (d) Outside the set-based model; choice from lists is taken up in Problem 6. (e) Not rational in general: the median of a menu can violate condition α.
